title: Introduce prefetch quarantine and grace window to resolve long-context tail escalation
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Several enterprise customers on Dedicated and Private deployments reported recurrent service degradation during correlated long-context request bursts. Root cause analysis points to an interaction between prefetch heuristics and admission that causes a wave of very long-context requests to monopolize the KV cache and scheduler slots, starving latency-sensitive short requests and amplifying tail latency. This ticket implements a quarantine for aggressive prefetches and a short grace window for preemptive admission so that mixed-length workloads do not cause queue starvation or long-context tail saturation.
reproduction_steps: 1) Deploy runtime-1.24 with continuous-batcher enabled on a 4-GPU host
2) Replay customer trace (trace id: CUST-88-202602-1) using loaddriver with 75% short (<=128 tokens) + 25% long (>=4096 tokens) correlated bursts
3) Observe scheduler admission logs (metric: scheduler.admission.wait_ms) and kv-store eviction rate (metric: kv.evictions/s),
4) Notice that after ~120s the system enters sustained high tail latency for short requests and kv.evictions spike to >500/s
investigation_log: 2026-03-02 09:15 - Initial triage: Customer A escalation received (support ticket #SUP-2026-211). Noted pattern matches other mixed-length incidents but escalated due to Dedicated SLA breach.

2026-03-03 14:40 - Reproduced locally with customer's trace. Captured heap snapshots and scheduler timelines. Observed contiguous prefetch goroutines holding KV locks while admission window closed to new small requests.
2026-03-04 11:10 - Hypothesis: aggressive prefetch + admission hysteresis leads to head-of-line long batches that prevent preemptive dequeues of smaller latency-sensitive batches.
2026-03-05 16:00 - Spike experiment: disabled prefetching in runtime binary; short-request tail dropped by 72% in replay. Confirms prefetch coupling as root contributor.

2026-03-06 10:30 - Measured eviction churn correlated with long-request admission rate. KV cache retention mis-accounting found in evictor metrics; added metrics to capture per-tenant reservation hit rate.

2026-03-08 09:00 - Design review with PM (Elena Gomez) and SRE (Vikram Rao). Agreed approach: quarantine prefetches (bounded concurrency + soft timeout) + add 250ms grace window enabling preemptive admission for small requests preceding admitted long batches.
2026-03-09 15:20 - POC implemented in feature branch: feature/prefetch-quarantine. Bench run shows mixed workload 95th latency improvement for short requests from 420ms -> 110ms.
2026-03-11 17:45 - Customer A canary deployment scheduled on Dedicated pool 3 for 2h soak; SRE will monitor kv.evictions/s and scheduler.admission.preempt_count.
2026-03-12 08:30 - Canary initial results: preempt_count rose as expected, customer reported tangible UX improvement; further soak planned overnight.
decisions: Adopt quarantine window for prefetch tasks: limit concurrent aggressive prefetches per host to 4 and per-tenant to 2
Introduce a configurable grace window (default 250ms) that allows scheduler to accept/complete short requests before admitting a long-context batch
Do not disable prefetch entirely; instead degrade prefetch aggressiveness under eviction pressure to preserve model warmups without starving short flows
Expose runtime knobs via console and Dedicated config: prefetch_concurrency, prefetch_timeout_ms, admission_grace_ms
action_items: ENG: merge feature/prefetch-quarantine into release branch and add unit + integration tests (Marcus) - target: 2026-03-14
SRE: monitor canary dashboards and alert thresholds for kv.evictions/s > 200 (Vikram) - ongoing
PM: prepare customer communication and mitigation guidance for Private deployers (Elena) - draft due 2026-03-13
DX: add console toggles and tooltip copy for new knobs (Jordan Lee) - estimate 3 points
rollout_plan: 1) Merge change behind runtime feature flag: prefetch_quarantine_v1
2) Canary on Dedicated pool 3 for 2h with synthetic replay + customer trace (Customer A), monitor eviction and preempt metrics
3) If metrics stable, enable on remaining Dedicated pools over 4-hour rolling windows
4) Offer opt-in for Private deployments via release notes and a config flag; default enabled for Hosted
5) Post-deployment: 48h elevated monitoring with SRE runbook
test_plan: Unit tests for prefetch concurrency limiter and timeout behavior
Integration tests simulating mixed-length replay with admission grace window assertions
Load test: rps scaled to customer production rates, verify short-request 95th latency improves and kv.evictions decrease
Chaos test: inject network pause to prefetch goroutine path and ensure system degrades gracefully
rollback_plan: If canary exhibits increased short-request tail or higher kv.evictions than baseline for 30m, flip feature flag off and revert runtime image to previous canary; open postmortem with customer and SRE.
notes: This approach aims to keep benefits of warm prefetched KV entries while protecting short, latency-sensitive traffic.
We may follow up with tenant-aware admission reservoirs if churn persists after this mitigation.
Related customer complaints referenced: SUP-2026-211 (Customer A), SUP-2026-218 (Customer B on Private).
